It lists per-exchange permissions: Binance (Spot & Margin Trading and Futures, restrict to trusted IPs), OKX (Trade), Bybit (Read-Write plus Unified Trading), Kraken, KuCoin (Spot Trading), Gate (Read and Write), Bitget (Read-write), Coinbase (Trade). It recommends using the whitelisted 3Commas IP addresses shown under My Exchanges > Add exchange (Gate keys without IP binding last only 90 days, and the guide tells KuCoin users to set IP restriction to 'No'). Another 3Commas help page says to use API keys only for 3Commas and not link the same exchange account to another trading service. Its security page says 'The IP whitelist can be used to restrict the API key to certain IP addresses'. Hyperliquid keys expire about six months after connecting.

incidents.title: Proposed US class action (Freeman et al. v. 3Commas Technologies OU, No. 4:23-cv-00101) alleges 3Commas did not encrypt stored API data, that the breach exposed at least 100,000 consumers and led to nearly $22 million in theft. These are allegations, not findings.
incidents.outcome: No ruling or settlement reported on the source page

incidents.title: API data leak: an anonymous poster published a sample of ~100,000 API keys. After first denying a leak and pointing to phishing, 3Commas confirmed on 2022-12-28 that 'the data in the files is true' and asked Binance, KuCoin and other exchanges to revoke all keys connected to 3Commas. Binance's CEO had urged users to disable keys. The FBI was reported to be investigating. 3Commas says it found no evidence of an insider, and the attackers claimed an employee sold the data.
incidents.amount: Traders reported ~$22M stolen (Decrypt); ZachXBT verified 44 victims / $14.8M (Decrypt); HAPI counted 86 victims / $27.3M (ForkLog)
incidents.outcome: 3Commas urged all users to reissue keys and promised no reimbursement until its investigation ended; HAPI says all exchanges have since disabled 3Commas keys. We found no source for any 3Commas compensation.

incidents.title: Phishing: lookalike sites captured users' exchange API keys, which were used to place ~20,000 unauthorized trades (DMG and other tokens) on several exchanges. 3Commas said its own systems were not breached at the time; the Dec 2022 leak later contradicted that.
incidents.outcome: FTX agreed a one-time ~$6M payout (Blockworks); 3Commas reported cloned sites for takedown

checks.worst_case: 3Commas holds API keys that can trade on your exchange account. If they leak (as ~100,000 did in Dec 2022) or are phished, attackers can place orders that drain your balance even without withdrawal rights, and 3Commas' terms cap its liability at the subscription price you paid. A key with withdrawal enabled could be emptied outright.
safe_setup: Open 3Commas only from 3commas.io (bookmark it) and turn on 2FA on both 3Commas and your exchange; never enter API keys on a site reached from ads, search results or DMs

Create the exchange API key with trading permission only and withdrawals disabled, restricted to the 3Commas IP addresses shown under My Exchanges > Add exchange (use a dedicated sub-account where your exchange supports it), and use the key only for 3Commas
Keep only the balance your bots need on that exchange account, and revoke the key at the exchange (not just in 3Commas) if you stop using it or suspect a leak

custody.note: Custodial exchange. Pionex says it keeps '100% reserve' and uses a Merkle tree plus an independent audit to show it; these are Pionex's own claims, and we did not find the audit report itself.

can_move_funds_out.note: Pionex says 'users can withdraw their coins at any time', and its help center has withdrawal guides for web and app. Trustpilot reviewers report withdrawals blocked during Pionex 'risk-control' reviews or until KYC is completed (user claims, not verified).

freeze_policy.note: Pionex's terms of use could not be retrieved, so the exact wording is not confirmed here. In public replies on Trustpilot, Pionex cites 'risk-control measures' when users report funds being unavailable, and reviewers describe trading and withdrawal restrictions followed by requests for personal and trading records.

api_keys.note: Pionex's API docs recommend setting up IP whitelisting along with the API key. Keys are created in the app or site under Account Settings, API Management (per CoinLedger's guide). The docs link to a separate 'API Key Permissions' page, which could not be retrieved, so whether keys have a withdrawal permission is not confirmed. Third-party guides say read-only keys are enough for tax and portfolio tools (CoinLedger, TradesViz).

incidents.title: Four US state regulators (Nebraska, North Carolina, Ohio, South Dakota) issued a consent order against Pionex Inc., the US entity, over failing to collect sender and beneficiary information on transfers above $3,000, information-security and record-keeping deficiencies, and operating before licensing in North Carolina and Ohio. Pionex did not admit wrongdoing.
incidents.outcome: Penalty plus two years of quarterly progress reports; no cease-and-desist

incidents.title: Pionex was attacked and suspended deposits and withdrawals while it repaired and upgraded its wallet functions (Wu Blockchain report, per CoinCodeCap). The article does not say how much was lost.
incidents.outcome: Per the article, Pionex said it had fully compensated affected users and would reopen deposits and withdrawals after the upgrade. We did not find Pionex's own notice.

incidents.title: Pattern of user complaints: Trustpilot shows a 2.5/5 score from 636 reviews (40% one-star). Themes include stuck withdrawals, trading and withdrawal restrictions after profitable trades or deposits, KYC-gated withdrawals, slow support and disputed compensation. Trustpilot does not verify reviews.
incidents.outcome: Pionex replies to most negative reviews, often citing risk-control measures; compensation limited to verified platform issues

checks.worst_case: Pionex holds your coins, so an exchange hack or insolvency, or an account restriction after a 'risk-control' review, could lock your balance and your running bots for an unknown time. The '100% reserve' claim is Pionex's own, and you would depend on Pionex's compensation decisions.
safe_setup: Type pionex.com yourself or use a bookmark; treat any Telegram or X DM, 'support' contact or giveaway as a scam, and join only the group linked from the site (t.me/pionexen)
Create API keys under Account Settings, API Management, bind each key to your bot's IP as the docs recommend, and enable only the permissions the bot needs
Keep only trading capital on Pionex and check your balance against its Merkle tree page; hold savings in your own wallet
